synthesis: The period integral packages the critical modular-form L-values as coefficients of one polynomial. Applying the completed L-function's functional equation to those coefficients gives a reciprocal relation and hence an invariant circle for the polynomial's root pairing. A half-polynomial removes the redundant reciprocal half; on the unit circle its reflected sum becomes a real sine or cosine polynomial, so proving the required number of sign changes, together with degree and multiplicity accounting, proves that every period-polynomial root lies on the circle.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2237579816_v2_u01 defines the completed L-function, period integral, and coefficient expansion of r_f in critical values. Unit u02 derives the reciprocal polynomial relation and root pairing from the functional equation and states Theorem 1.1. Unit u03 defines P_f, reconstructs a rescaled r_f from P_f(z)+epsilon(f)P_f(1/z), and reduces the unit-circle theorem to the required sine- or cosine-polynomial sign changes.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis composes three representation changes: critical values become polynomial coefficients, the s-to-k-s functional symmetry becomes inversion in the polynomial variable, and reciprocal pairing becomes a real boundary trace whose sign changes certify complex roots. This dependency chain is not contained in any one parent.
limits: Reciprocal pairing alone does not force circle membership; the proof still owes a complete sign-change count and degree/multiplicity accounting. The theorem concerns zeros of period polynomials, not zeros of the Riemann zeta function or of the modular L-function, and the phrase 'Riemann hypothesis' is only an analogy. Level square roots, signs, powers of i, coefficient indices, scaling, and exact phase formulas are OCR- and representation-sensitive and require the PDF. No cross-object implication or novelty claim is supported.
quality_reason: Accepted because all three parents support a concrete end-to-end reduction from L-value data to a real-variable root count, while the synthesis keeps reciprocal symmetry distinct from the later theorem that all roots lie on the invariant circle.

synthesis: Two analytic inputs constrain the critical values that become trigonometric coefficients. Grouped Hadamard factors and the known zero strip make completed critical values monotone without assuming the modular L-function RH, while Euler-product estimates give form-uniform bounds for ratios of uncompleted L-values in the absolute-convergence range. After the period-polynomial normalization, these inequalities supply the increasing nonnegative coefficient conditions required by the Pólya-Szegő sign-change criterion. Weight six instead needs specialized adjacent-value product inequalities, obtained by grouping complete zero orbits, because the general monotone-coefficient route is not the whole argument there.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2237579816_v2_u05 derives monotonicity of Lambda(f,s) to the right of the zero strip from paired Hadamard factors. Unit u06 bounds L-value ratios uniformly by a squared zeta-value ratio using the Euler-product logarithmic derivative and Ramanujan-Deligne bounds. Unit u11 translates Pólya-Szegő's increasing-coefficient condition into binomially weighted completed-L inequalities and then into explicit level thresholds. Unit u09 supplies the different grouped-zero-factor inequalities used for the exceptional weight-six coefficient geometry.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis traces zero geometry through two different analytic transformations into polynomial coefficient geometry and then into a topological zero count: zero-strip confinement yields order, Euler factors yield uniform ratio control, and the trigonometric theorem consumes both after normalization. It also identifies the specialized grouped-factor branch rather than pretending the sufficient monotonicity criterion covers every case.
limits: The Hadamard argument uses known strip confinement and symmetry, not RH, and the zeta function appears only as a majorant in the absolute-convergence estimate; neither input says anything about zeta zeros. Pólya-Szegő monotonicity is sufficient, not necessary, and it fails for some forms whose period-polynomial roots still lie on the circle. Exact factor groupings, normalized inequalities, binomial ratios, zeta powers, thresholds, and endpoint conventions are extraction-sensitive. Reported finite Sage checks are not reproduced in these parents, and no general transfer beyond the stated modular-form family is established.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents jointly establish a specific analytic-to-coefficient-to-zero-count pipeline and also document its boundary: low-weight product inequalities and residual cases require arguments beyond the uniform monotone-coefficient criterion.

synthesis: For weight six with even functional-equation sign, the unit-circle root count reduces to two inequalities among Lambda(f,3), Lambda(f,4), and Lambda(f,5). The paper proves those obligations unconditionally by checking compatible inequalities on every real, critical-line, and off-line zero orbit in the Hadamard product and multiplying the resulting local certificates. Separately, assuming RH for the completed modular L-function, symmetry and nonnegativity of even central Taylor coefficients give a conceptual proof of the boundary inequality (4.2). The conditional Taylor account explains one sign invariant but is not the theorem's unconditional evidence.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2237579816_v2_u08 derives the two weight-six inequalities (4.2) and (4.3) from the signs at the trigonometric polynomial's extrema. Unit u09 proves both obligations through an elementary product lemma and Hadamard zero groups, explicitly including off-critical-line orbits. Unit u10 assumes modular-L RH and uses the central Taylor expansion to derive (4.2) from vanishing odd derivatives and nonnegative even derivatives.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis aligns two logically different routes to the same boundary sign: a zero-orbit multiplication proof valid without RH and a conditional Taylor-positivity explanation. Comparing them reveals which part is theorem, which part is conditional interpretation, and why the latter cannot replace or validate the former.
limits: The Taylor route is explicitly conditional on RH for Lambda(f,s) and cannot be used as evidence for that hypothesis or for the Riemann zeta RH. In the supplied unit it explains (4.2), not the separate obligation (4.3). The unconditional proof depends on Hadamard convergence, known zero symmetries, nonnegativity, and exact per-orbit algebra. Multiplicities, absolute-value factors, derivative superscripts, factorials, equality conventions, and Taylor coefficients are formula-sensitive and require PDF verification. No converse, heuristic evidence for RH, or broader analogy is justified.
quality_reason: Accepted with the conditional scope narrowed to inequality (4.2). The three parents jointly support a valuable proof-versus-explanation distinction while preserving the independent second inequality and all hypothesis burdens.

synthesis: After normalizing P_f to Q_f, the large-weight argument separates an explicit exponential model from three errors. On the unit circle the model's phase must be monotone so that its alternating extrema enumerate the required sign intervals; independently, the total error must be strictly smaller than the model's minimum amplitude so those signs survive for Q_f. Explicit bounds on coefficient error, exponential-tail error, and the central term turn this into weight-level thresholds. A later, sharper uniform approximation and two-sided tests around each model phase zero then trap one true root nearby, upgrading the global circle count to asymptotic localization.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2237579816_v2_u12 gives the model-plus-three-errors decomposition, the unit-circle phase, and the strict amplitude-versus-error criterion for preserving all real- or imaginary-part sign changes. Unit u13 bounds the three errors by different analytic inputs and combines them into a sufficient threshold inequality. Unit u14 applies the asymptotic phase approximation on both sides of each predicted phase zero and transfers the trapped zeros back to r_f for the two functional-equation signs.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis separates two stability certificates and then strengthens their output: phase monotonicity orders the model zeros, amplitude control preserves the count under perturbation, and local two-sided sign stability matches individual true roots to predicted phases. Neither a small error alone nor an unperturbed phase count alone supplies the full conclusion.
limits: The count requires the applicable large-weight phase regime and a strict numerical error bound; the localization additionally requires sufficiently large combined parameters and is asymptotic, not an exact formula for every weight and level. The threshold estimates are sufficient rather than necessary, and the displayed central-term bound has its own lower-weight condition. Summation limits, central term, square-root level factors, phase derivative, error constants, table entries, neighborhood widths, and the back-transformation are OCR- and formula-sensitive. This perturbative mechanism concerns period-polynomial roots only and licenses no spectral or zeta-zero analogy.
quality_reason: Accepted because the three parents support a concrete progression from a zero-transparent model, through independently bounded perturbations, to both complete zero counting and root-by-root localization. The synthesis retains the distinct parameter burdens for count and localization.

synthesis: The paper partitions the proof into two sufficient analytic regions and a reported finite computational remainder. A Pólya-Szegő coefficient criterion covers moderate weights at sufficiently large level, while the exponential-model error budget covers larger weights and complementary level ranges. For the remaining newforms, the authors report high-precision critical-L evaluation, first testing the sufficient coefficient inequalities and, when those fail, directly checking the required trigonometric sign changes rather than treating criterion failure as theorem failure.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2237579816_v2_u11 gives explicit sufficient level bounds from the Pólya-Szegő coefficient criterion and reports Sage checks below them. Unit u13 supplies the second sufficient inequality, its threshold table, and another reported finite Sage remainder. Unit u15 describes the residual weight-level ranges, Sage enumeration of newforms, high-precision L-value evaluation, coefficient tests, direct sign-change checks for failures, and one worked example.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis combines complementary analytic coverage maps with a targeted computational fallback: theorem cases outside both sufficient regions are enumerated, and the final check returns to the same boundary sign-change certificate used by the proof. This distinguishes failure of an analytic sufficient condition from failure of the circle-root statement.
limits: Quarantined because the computational closure is central to the claimed exhaustive theorem coverage but is not reproducible or error-certified from the supplied source. The text preserves no Sage version, commands, exact precision targets, rounding bounds, exhaustive machine-readable case manifest, or complete outputs; one worked example cannot certify every residual form. Threshold constants, table alignment, decimal L-values, trigonometric coefficients, and sign intervals are also extraction-sensitive. The analytic regions remain supported as sufficient regions, and the paper's computation is honestly reported as provenance, but it is not independent computational evidence here. No inference about L-function or zeta zeros is allowed.
quality_reason: Quarantined rather than rejected: the three units jointly support the stated proof architecture and the authors' report of finite computation, but the source defect prevents auditing the exhaustive residual closure at the evidentiary level required for acceptance.
